title: Weights of a rational module generated by a Borel eigenvector
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq G$, a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, its unipotent radical $U$, the projection $p:B\to T$ and the simple roots $\Delta\subseteq X^*(T)$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional rational $G$-module, meaning an $F$-vector space with an $F$-linear coaction $c:M\to M\otimes_F F[G]$ satisfying coassociativity and the counit identity. A rational submodule is a linear subspace $N$ with $c(N)\subseteq N\otimes_F F[G]$. Let $\lambda:T\to\mathbf G_m$ be a character and $0\ne v\in M$ such that $b(v\otimes1)=\lambda(p(b))(v\otimes1)$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $b\in B(A)$. Assume the smallest rational $G$-submodule of $M$ containing $v$ is $M$. For $\mu\in X^*(T)$ write $M_\mu=\{m:t(m\otimes1)=\mu(t)(m\otimes1)\text{ for every }A\text{ and }t\in T(A)\}$. Then $M_\lambda=Fv$, and for every $\mu$ with $M_\mu\ne0$ there are integers $n_\alpha\ge0$ such that $\mu=\lambda-\sum_{\alpha\in\Delta}n_\alpha\alpha$. No simplicity or characteristic-zero hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put $R=F[G]$ and let $D$ be the coefficient subspace of $c(v)$: the span of $(1\otimes\varphi)c(v)$ for $F$-linear $\varphi:R\to F$. Choose a finite expression $c(v)=\sum_j d_j\otimes f_j$ with the $f_j$ linearly independent, so $D=\operatorname{span}_F\{d_j\}$. Coassociativity gives $\sum_j c(d_j)\otimes f_j=\sum_j d_j\otimes\Delta_R(f_j)$. Applying on the last factor a linear functional taking $f_j$ to $1$ and the other $f_i$ to $0$ shows $c(d_j)\in D\otimes_F R$. The counit gives $v=\sum_j\varepsilon(f_j)d_j\in D$. Thus $D$ is a rational submodule containing $v$, so the cyclicity assumption implies $D=M$. This is the coaction form of the orbit span used in the source.

proof.text:
Expand the regular orbit map on these affine coordinates as the finite vector-valued polynomial
$$f(z)=x_1(z_1)\cdots x_r(z_r)v=\sum_{I\in\mathbf N^r}z^I m_I.$$
Its constant term is $m_0=v$, since each $x_i(0)=1$. Because $t v=\lambda(t)v$ and each $x_i$ has conjugation character $\beta_i$, the preceding formulas give
$$t f(z)=\lambda(t) f(\beta_1(t)z_1,\ldots,\beta_r(t)z_r).$$
For an arbitrary commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $t\in T(A)$, compare coefficients in $(M\otimes_F A)[z_1,\ldots,z_r]$. This yields $t(m_I\otimes1)=\lambda(t)\prod_i\beta_i(t)^{I_i}(m_I\otimes1)$. Thus every nonzero $m_I$ is a weight vector of character $\nu_I=\lambda+\sum_i I_i\beta_i$. This is precisely the coefficient comparison of Milne 22.14, applied to the entire finite product; it uses polynomial identities, with no division by factorials.

source.place: Proposition 22.14 and its proof, p.466, coefficient comparison; Proposition 22.17, p.467, iterating negative root actions.

proof.text: Let $C=\operatorname{span}_F\{m_I\}\subseteq M$ and $q:M\to M/C$. On the affine chart $U^-\times_F B\simeq U^-B$ the orbit map $g\mapsto gv$ equals $(z,b)\mapsto\lambda(p(b)) f(z)$. Hence its composite with $q$ vanishes as a morphism of schemes, not just at $F$-points. Apply [lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic] to the dense open immersion $j:U^-B\hookrightarrow G$. Its target is reduced by step 2; both source and target are affine (the source is $\mathbf A_F^r\times_F B$), so $j$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its scheme-theoretic image is $G$. By [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], for this quasi-compact $j$ the kernel of $\mathcal O_G\to j_*\mathcal O_{U^-B}$ is therefore zero. Restriction $R\to\Gamma(U^-B,\mathcal O)$ is injective. Apply this to each coordinate of $q(gv)$ to get $(q\otimes1)c(v)=0$. Thus $c(v)\in C\otimes_F R$, so every coefficient of $c(v)$ lies in $C$. Step 1 gives $M=D\subseteq C$, whence $M=C$.

Step 2 repairs this via n0^2 in T(F). Step 1 (coefficient span D of c(v) is rational and contains v, so D=M) checks by coassociativity and counit. Step 2: the Bruhat cell-charts node gives an involutive w0, the open dense C_{w0}=V n0 B with V^{w0}=V, and G geometrically integral; the new node plus the u_alpha formula gives A^r = U^- with t x_i(z) t^-1 = x_i(beta_i(t) z) and beta_i = w0 alpha_i in -Phi+. Step 4: the Nagata reduced-density lemma applies (G reduced; open immersion of affines, hence qc and qs; dense image), and the definition gives zero kernel for quasi-compact j; so restriction is injective, M=C.
